outcome: Self-reported behaviour change (alcohol consumption, frequent weight monitoring, preconception supplementation, cervical cancer screening)
cohort: The study included 298 Australian women actively planning a pregnancy, with a mean age of 31.8 years and a mean BMI of 25.7 kg/m(2).
finding: The OptimalMe digital health intervention with coaching led to statistically significant improvements in preconception behaviours such as reduced alcohol consumption, increased preconception supplementation, and more frequent weight monitoring, alongside improved healthcare engagement.
